# jscent API reference

<!-- Generated by gen/api_docs.ts from the type declarations: `npm run docs`. Do not edit. -->

The public API of jscent, from its doc comments. The [README](README.md) shows how to use it; the request and result types come from Centrifugo's protos, with their documentation.

## jscent

The client, batches, results and helpers.

### `Client`

```ts
new Client(options: ClientOptions)
```

Calls Centrifugo's HTTP server API. Create it once and share it: it is
safe for concurrent use.

```ts
const client = new Client({ apiEndpoint: 'http://localhost:8000/api', apiKey: process.env.CENTRIFUGO_API_KEY });
await client.publish({ channel: 'news', data: { text: 'hello' } });
```

Every API method takes its request and resolves to its result, rejecting
unless Centrifugo did everything asked. Each takes `{ timeout, signal }`;
without a timeout, requestTimeout bounds the call.

#### `blockUser(request: BlockUserRequest, options?: CallOptions): Promise<BlockUserResult>`

Blocks a user: the user is disconnected and can not
connect again until unblocked or the block expires. Centrifugo PRO only.

#### `broadcast(request: BroadcastRequest, options?: CallOptions): Promise<BroadcastResult>`

Publishes the same data into many channels in one request.

Channels succeed or fail on their own. It resolves when every channel got
the publication. When Centrifugo carried the broadcast out and one or more
channels failed - up to all of them - it rejects with
BroadcastFailedChannelsError, whose `result` holds every channel's
outcome. Any other error means it failed as a whole: no channel got a
reply. After a timeout or a network error Centrifugo may still have
published it.

To go on despite some failed channels:

```ts
try {
  await client.broadcast(request);
} catch (e) {
  if (!(e instanceof BroadcastFailedChannelsError)) throw e;
  logger.warn('broadcast failed in some channels', e.result.failed);
}
```

Retry it with broadcastWithRetry, which sends again only the channels
which may still succeed, with one idempotencyKey.

#### `broadcastWithRetry(request: BroadcastRequest, options?: BroadcastRetryOptions): Promise<BroadcastResult>`

Broadcasts as broadcast does, and retries the channels which failed for a
temporary reason - see retryable - up to maxAttempts (2 by default: one
retry).

- Only the channels which may still succeed are sent again; when only
  channels which failed for good are left, it stops.
- Every attempt carries the same idempotencyKey - made for the call when
  the request has none - so that a channel which got the publication in an
  earlier attempt does not get it again. The memory, Redis and PostgreSQL
  brokers keep keys; the NATS broker ignores them, and a retry may publish
  again.
- The result holds every channel's last outcome, and the key: retrying
  later with it publishes only into the channels which did not get it.

`timeout`, when set, bounds the whole call, waits included;
`attemptTimeout` - requestTimeout by default - bounds each attempt.
`onAttemptError` decides the wait between attempts, and may stop them. It
rejects as broadcast does.

#### `cancelPush(request: CancelPushRequest, options?: CallOptions): Promise<CancelPushResult>`

Cancels a delayed push notification (sent with
`sendAt`). Centrifugo PRO only.

#### `channels(request: ChannelsRequest, options?: CallOptions): Promise<ChannelsResult>`

Returns active channels (with one or more subscribers).
It can be heavy on large deployments: there is no pagination.

#### `close(options?: { timeout?: number; }): Promise<void>`

Stops the client: calls made from now on reject with ClosedError, and
close waits for the calls in progress to end - automatic batches
included. A broadcast being retried stops at its next attempt. With
`timeout`, in milliseconds, it rejects with TimeoutError when calls are
still in progress then; they go on, and close may be called again.

Call it when the application shuts down, so that what was accepted is
sent before the process exits.

#### `connections(request: ConnectionsRequest, options?: CallOptions): Promise<ConnectionsResult>`

Returns information about active connections, without
the need to enable presence. At least one of user, expression or
`labelFilter` must be set. Centrifugo PRO only.

#### `deleteUserStatus(request: DeleteUserStatusRequest, options?: CallOptions): Promise<DeleteUserStatusResult>`

Deletes the status of users. Centrifugo PRO only.

#### `deviceList(request: DeviceListRequest, options?: CallOptions): Promise<DeviceListResult>`

Returns a paginated list of registered devices.
Centrifugo PRO only.

#### `deviceRegister(request: DeviceRegisterRequest, options?: CallOptions): Promise<DeviceRegisterResult>`

Registers a device for push notifications, or
updates a registered one. Centrifugo PRO only.

#### `deviceRemove(request: DeviceRemoveRequest, options?: CallOptions): Promise<DeviceRemoveResult>`

Removes devices, selected by ids and/or users.
Centrifugo PRO only.

#### `deviceTopicList(request: DeviceTopicListRequest, options?: CallOptions): Promise<DeviceTopicListResult>`

Returns a paginated list of device topic
subscriptions. Centrifugo PRO only.

#### `deviceTopicUpdate(request: DeviceTopicUpdateRequest, options?: CallOptions): Promise<DeviceTopicUpdateResult>`

Changes the topics of a device. The device topic
list is what decides who gets a push sent to a topic.
Centrifugo PRO only.

#### `deviceUpdate(request: DeviceUpdateRequest, options?: CallOptions): Promise<DeviceUpdateResult>`

Updates registered devices, selected by ids and/or
users. Centrifugo PRO only.

#### `disconnect(request: DisconnectRequest, options?: CallOptions): Promise<DisconnectResult>`

Disconnects a user's connections.

#### `getUserStatus(request: GetUserStatusRequest, options?: CallOptions): Promise<GetUserStatusResult>`

Returns the status of users. Centrifugo PRO only.

#### `history(request: HistoryRequest, options?: CallOptions): Promise<HistoryResult>`

Returns publications from the history of a channel.
History must be enabled for the channel.

#### `historyRemove(request: HistoryRemoveRequest, options?: CallOptions): Promise<HistoryRemoveResult>`

Removes publications from the history of a channel.
The current top stream position is kept, so clients do not get
disconnected because of insufficient state.

#### `info(request?: InfoRequest, options?: CallOptions): Promise<InfoResult>`

Returns information about the running Centrifugo nodes.

#### `invalidateUserTokens(request: InvalidateUserTokensRequest, options?: CallOptions): Promise<InvalidateUserTokensResult>`

Revokes all tokens of a user issued before a
certain time (based on the iat claim of a JWT). Centrifugo PRO only.

#### `mapClear(request: MapClearRequest, options?: CallOptions): Promise<MapClearResult>`

Removes all state and stream data of a map channel.

#### `mapPublish(request: MapPublishRequest, options?: CallOptions): Promise<MapPublishResult>`

Publishes or updates a key in a map channel.

#### `mapReadState(request: MapReadStateRequest, options?: CallOptions): Promise<MapReadStateResult>`

Reads the current state of a map channel, with
optional pagination.

#### `mapReadStream(request: MapReadStreamRequest, options?: CallOptions): Promise<MapReadStreamResult>`

Reads the change stream of a map channel.

#### `mapRemove(request: MapRemoveRequest, options?: CallOptions): Promise<MapRemoveResult>`

Removes a key from a map channel.

#### `mapStats(request: MapStatsRequest, options?: CallOptions): Promise<MapStatsResult>`

Returns statistics about a map channel.

#### `newBatch(options?: { parallel?: boolean; }): Batch`

An empty Batch sent by this client. Without `parallel` the commands run
one by one, in the order added - but Centrifugo PRO sends a sequential
batch's publications to its broker together: each channel's take effect in
order, publications into different channels may not, unless the
namespace sets publication_grouping_disabled. With `parallel`, Centrifugo
runs them concurrently, with no order.

#### `presence(request: PresenceRequest, options?: CallOptions): Promise<PresenceResult>`

Returns the online presence of a channel: all clients
currently subscribed to it. Presence must be enabled for the channel.

#### `presenceStats(request: PresenceStatsRequest, options?: CallOptions): Promise<PresenceStatsResult>`

Returns short presence information of a channel: the
number of clients and of unique users. Presence must be enabled for the
channel.

#### `publish(request: PublishRequest, options?: CallOptions): Promise<PublishResult>`

Publishes data into a channel.

#### `refresh(request: RefreshRequest, options?: CallOptions): Promise<RefreshResult>`

Refreshes a user's connections, mostly useful with
unidirectional transports. Without `expireAt` the connections become
non-expiring.

#### `revokeToken(request: RevokeTokenRequest, options?: CallOptions): Promise<RevokeTokenResult>`

Revokes a token by its unique ID (jti claim of a JWT).
Clients using the token are disconnected shortly, and can not connect
with it again. Centrifugo PRO only.

#### `sendPushNotification(request: SendPushNotificationRequest, options?: CallOptions): Promise<SendPushNotificationResult>`

Sends a push notification. The request is
queued and sent to the provider by Centrifugo workers.
Centrifugo PRO only.

#### `sharedPollPublish(request: SharedPollPublishRequest, options?: CallOptions): Promise<SharedPollPublishResult>`

Pushes data for a key directly to clients of a
shared poll channel, without waiting for the next poll cycle. Requires
versioned mode and publish_enabled on the namespace.

#### `subscribe(request: SubscribeRequest, options?: CallOptions): Promise<SubscribeResult>`

Subscribes active sessions of a user to a channel
(server-side subscription). It does not create a streaming subscription
for the caller.

#### `unblockUser(request: UnblockUserRequest, options?: CallOptions): Promise<UnblockUserResult>`

Unblocks a user. Centrifugo PRO only.

#### `unsubscribe(request: UnsubscribeRequest, options?: CallOptions): Promise<UnsubscribeResult>`

Unsubscribes a user from a channel.

#### `updatePushStatus(request: UpdatePushStatusRequest, options?: CallOptions): Promise<UpdatePushStatusResult>`

Saves the delivery or interaction status of a
push notification to analytics. Experimental. Centrifugo PRO only.

#### `updateUserStatus(request: UpdateUserStatusRequest, options?: CallOptions): Promise<UpdateUserStatusResult>`

Marks users as active and online now, and sets
their state when one is given. Centrifugo PRO only.

#### `userTopicList(request: UserTopicListRequest, options?: CallOptions): Promise<UserTopicListResult>`

Returns a paginated list of user topic
subscriptions. Centrifugo PRO only.

#### `userTopicUpdate(request: UserTopicUpdateRequest, options?: CallOptions): Promise<UserTopicUpdateResult>`

Changes the topics of a user. The change is also
applied to the user's registered devices. Centrifugo PRO only.

### interface `ClientOptions`

The options of a Client.

- `apiEndpoint?: string` - The base URL of the API, "http://localhost:8000/api". Each method is sent to it plus its name, "/publish".
- `getApiEndpoint?: () => string | Promise<string>` - Instead of apiEndpoint, returns it for each request, for addresses discovered rather than fixed.
- `apiKey?: string` - Sent as X-API-Key. Leave it and getBearerToken unset when requests are authenticated another way - mutual TLS, a proxy - or not at all.
- `getBearerToken?: () => string | Promise<string>` - Returns the token sent as "Authorization: Bearer" with each request, for Centrifugo PRO's JWKS authentication of the API - an ApiTokens's token, say. Not together with apiKey.
- `fetch?: Fetch` - The fetch sending the requests: the runtime's own by default. Pass your own - with an undici dispatcher, say, or instrumented for tracing. It is called with each request's credentials and headers, never changed.
- `requestTimeout?: number` - Milliseconds bounding a call without a timeout of its own: 10 seconds by default.
- `headers?: Record<string, string>` - Extra headers for every request, for a proxy in front of Centrifugo. Not X-API-Key, Authorization or Content-Type. A User-Agent replaces jscent's.
- `onRequest?: (info: RequestInfo) => void` - Called after every HTTP request, for metrics; the call waits for it. It must not throw: what it throws rejects the call in place of its outcome.
- `autoBatch?: AutoBatch` - Sends calls made concurrently in batches: see AutoBatch.
- `bigIntegers?: boolean` - Decodes integers past 2^53 in payloads as bigint, as centrifuge-js does: false by default, when they are rounded to the nearest number. See the README before turning it on: a field's type then follows its value.

### interface `AutoBatch`

Automatic batching: concurrent calls sent together, as one batch request,
once enough of them are in flight.

Nothing waits for a batch to fill. While fewer than maxInFlight requests
are in flight, every call is sent at once, alone, exactly as without it.
Only a call made when maxInFlight requests are already in flight waits -
for one of them to finish, not for a timer. Then all the calls waiting at
that moment go out together, at most maxBatchSize of them. The busier the
client, the larger the batches, and the fewer requests Centrifugo handles
for the same work.

Every call gets its own command's reply. Calls sharing a batch share its
request, though: when it fails as a whole - the network, the credentials, a
body too large for a proxy in front of Centrifugo (nginx refuses bodies
over 1 MB by default) - every call in it fails with that error.

- `maxInFlight: number` - How many requests may be in flight before calls start to wait and be batched: about half the calls the process makes at once. Above that, it never batches; just below, it batches calls one at a time, and only limits them.
- `maxBatchSize?: number` - The most calls one batch carries: 1000 by default.

### interface `BroadcastRetryOptions`

The options of broadcastWithRetry.

- `maxAttempts?: number` - How many attempts at most: 2 by default, one retry.
- `attemptTimeout?: number` - Milliseconds bounding each attempt: requestTimeout by default.
- `onAttemptError?: (attempt: BroadcastAttempt) => number | undefined | Promise<number | undefined>` - Called after an attempt which failed in a way a retry may fix, except the last. It returns the milliseconds to wait before the next attempt, or undefined for the default wait - exponentialBackoff(100, 5000) of the attempt - and may log or count meanwhile. To stop, it throws: its error propagates as it is. The wait never outlasts the call's timeout.

### interface `RequestInfo`

One HTTP request to Centrifugo's API, for onRequest.

- `readonly method: string` - The API method: "publish", say, or "batch" for a batch.
- `readonly commands: number` - How many commands the request carried: 1, or a batch's size.
- `readonly failed: number` - How many of them Centrifugo answered with an error. A broadcast which failed in some channels is not counted: its command was answered.
- `readonly autoBatch: boolean` - True for a batch made of concurrent calls by automatic batching.
- `readonly duration: number` - Milliseconds from before getting the endpoint and credentials to the reply read.
- `readonly status: number` - The HTTP status of the reply, 0 without one.
- `readonly error: Error | undefined` - The request's own error: the network, a timeout, an HTTP status, a reply which is not Centrifugo's, a request refused before sending - or, in the transport error mode, the error of its one command. Undefined when Centrifugo's reply was read.

### `Batch`

Commands sent to Centrifugo in one request. Create one with
`client.newBatch()`, add commands - a method per API method, each returning a
Pending - then send:

```ts
const batch = client.newBatch();
const pub = batch.publish({ channel: 'news', data: { text: 'hi' } });
const stats = batch.presenceStats({ channel: 'news' });
await batch.send();              // throws unless every command succeeded
pub.result().offset;
```

A batch is sent once, and is not safe for concurrent use.

#### `send(options?: CallOptions): Promise<BatchResult>`

Sends the batch and waits for Centrifugo's reply to every command.

It resolves when every command succeeded. BatchFailedCommandsError means
one or more commands failed, up to all: every command got its own reply,
each Pending holds its outcome. Any other error means the batch failed as
a whole: no command got a reply, and every Pending throws that error. A
command the client can tell is invalid fails the whole batch before
anything is sent. An empty batch sends nothing.

Adds a shared_poll_publish command: see Client.sharedPollPublish.

### `Pending`

The outcome of one command of a batch, available once the batch is sent.

#### `static resolved<T>(value: T): Pending<T>`

A Pending of no batch, whose result() returns value or throws error: for
test doubles of code which reads a batch's outcomes.

#### `static resolved<T = never>(value: undefined, error: Error): Pending<T>`

#### `result(): T`

The command's result, or its error thrown: an ApiError for this command,
the error which failed the whole batch, or BatchNotSentError. A broadcast
throws BroadcastFailedChannelsError, carrying every channel's outcome,
when any channel failed.

### `BatchResult`

```ts
new BatchResult(replied: boolean, failed?: FailedCommand[])
```

The outcome of a sent batch as a whole. Each command's own outcome is in the
Pending its method returned. JSON.stringify renders it as
`{replied, failed}`, each failed command as `{index, method, error}`, the
error as `{code, message}`.

- `readonly replied: boolean` - True when Centrifugo replied to every command, the failed ones included; false when the batch failed as a whole. True for an empty batch.

#### `get failed(): FailedCommand[]`

The commands which failed, with their errors, in the order they were added - as the error's failed lists them.

#### `toJSON(): Record<string, unknown>`

### interface `FailedCommand`

The failure of one command of a batch.

- `readonly index: number` - The command's position in the batch, from zero.
- `readonly method: string` - Its API method, such as "publish".
- `readonly error: Error` - The error its Pending throws: an ApiError, or a BroadcastFailedChannelsError for a broadcast which failed in one or more channels.

### `BroadcastResult`

```ts
new BroadcastResult(channels: ChannelResult[], idempotencyKey?: string, attempts?: number, replied?: boolean)
```

The outcome of a broadcast: one entry per channel, in the order the request
listed them. JSON.stringify renders it with Centrifugo's field names:
`{channels, idempotency_key, attempts, replied}`, each channel as
`{channel, result, error, attempts}` - result when it succeeded, error,
`{code, message}`, when it failed.

- `readonly channels: ChannelResult[]` - Every channel's outcome.
- `readonly idempotencyKey: string` - The key the broadcast was sent with: the request's, or the one broadcastWithRetry made when the request had none. A later retry with it does not publish again into the channels which got the publication.
- `readonly attempts: number` - How many times the broadcast was tried: 1 from broadcast, up to maxAttempts from broadcastWithRetry, 0 when it was refused before sending.
- `readonly replied: boolean` - True when Centrifugo carried the broadcast out and replied for every channel, the failed ones included; false when it failed as a whole.

#### `get failed(): ChannelResult[]`

The channels which did not get the publication, with their errors, in the order of the request.

#### `toJSON(): Record<string, unknown>`

### interface `ChannelResult`

The outcome of a broadcast in one channel.

- `readonly channel: string` - The channel, as the request named it.
- `readonly result: PublishResult | undefined` - The publication's position in the channel's history, when it succeeded.
- `readonly error: Error | undefined` - Undefined when the publication succeeded; the channel's ApiError, or the error of the whole broadcast when it failed as a whole.
- `readonly attempts: number` - How many times the channel was sent: more than 1 when broadcastWithRetry retried it.

### `RawJSON`

```ts
new RawJSON(text: string)
```

JSON text, sent as it is: a payload already encoded - from a database, a
queue, a cache - or encoded with rules of your own. It is checked to be
valid JSON when created, and sent unchanged, number text kept - also inside
another value:

    await client.publish({ channel: 'news', data: rawJSON(row.payload) });
    await client.publish({ channel: 'news', data: { meta, doc: rawJSON(row.doc) } });

A string, by contrast, is always a JSON string: `data: 'hi'` publishes "hi".

- `readonly text: string` - The JSON text.

#### `toJSON(): unknown`

Its value, for a JSON.stringify of your own: integers past 2^53 lose their digits there.

#### `toString(): string`

### `rawJSON`

```ts
function rawJSON(text: string): RawJSON;
```

JSON text, sent as it is: see RawJSON.

### interface `CallOptions`

The options of one call.

- `timeout?: number` - Milliseconds bounding the call - connecting, sending, the reply's headers and body: requestTimeout when unset.
- `signal?: AbortSignal` - Aborts the call; it then throws the signal's reason, as fetch does.

### `retryable`

```ts
function retryable(err: unknown): boolean;
```

Whether a new attempt, with time left, may succeed after `err`: the error
came from a temporary condition, not from the request.

Retryable are an ApiError Centrifugo marked temporary, and code 100 from
Centrifugo versions which did not mark errors yet; a network failure; a
timeout, also one of the caller's own signal; an HTTPError 429 or 5xx; a
broadcast or batch partial error with at least one retryable part.

Not retryable are the request's own errors - an unknown channel, a bad
request, InvalidRequestError - and InvalidConfigError, ClosedError, an
aborted call, a DecodeError and rejected credentials.

A retryable error does not mean nothing was done: retry a publication only
with the same idempotencyKey. Retry a broadcast with broadcastWithRetry, or
only its retryableChannels(): repeating the call resends to the channels
which already got it.

### `exponentialBackoff`

```ts
function exponentialBackoff(base: number, limit: number): (attempt: number) => number;
```

The wait, in milliseconds, before retrying after a failed attempt, attempt 1
being the first failure: `base` after it, twice as long after each next
one, up to `limit`. Each wait is a random time between half of it and all of
it, so that clients which failed together do not all retry at the same
moment. A negative base counts as zero, a limit below base as base, and an
attempt below 1 as 1.

In a retry loop of your own - a publication retried with the same
idempotencyKey:

```ts
const backoff = exponentialBackoff(100, 2_000);
for (let attempt = 1; ; attempt++) {
  try {
    return await client.publish(request);
  } catch (e) {
    if (!retryable(e) || attempt === 3) throw e;
  }
  await wait(backoff(attempt), signal);
}
```

Retry a broadcast with broadcastWithRetry instead: repeating it resends to
the channels which already got it.

### `wait`

```ts
function wait(ms: number, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<void>;
```

Waits `ms` milliseconds, or until `signal` aborts - then it throws the
signal's reason: the wait between retries, which a deadline or a
cancellation ends.

### interface `BroadcastAttempt`

A failed attempt of broadcastWithRetry, given to its onAttemptError.

- `readonly attempt: number` - The attempt which failed, from 1.
- `readonly error: Error` - Its error: BroadcastFailedChannelsError when Centrifugo replied and some channels failed, otherwise the error of the request as a whole.
- `readonly retry: ChannelResult[]` - The channels the next attempt sends, with the errors this attempt failed them with. A broadcast to many channels which all failed lists every one: log a count or a few.
- `readonly result: BroadcastResult` - Every channel's outcome so far, as the call would return it if it stopped now.
- `readonly idempotencyKey: string` - The key every attempt is sent with.

### `command`

```ts
const command: { publish(request: PublishRequest): Command; /* ...one per API method */ }
```

Commands for Centrifugo's async consumers, one per method of api.proto: each
checks its request as a call does, and encodes it. See Command.

```ts
const cmd = command.publish({ channel: 'news', data: { text: 'hi' } });
```

### interface `Command`

An API call left for Centrifugo's async consumers to make: written to a
PostgreSQL outbox table, a Kafka topic, a Redis stream - made with
`command.publish({ ... })` and the like. See
https://centrifugal.dev/docs/server/consumers.

Consumers take it as its method and payload apart - the outbox table's
method and payload columns, a message attribute - or as the JSON message
`{"method": ..., "payload": ...}` of toString (Kafka, NATS JetStream).
JSON.stringify gives that message too, also of a command inside another
value, with payload as a JSON object.

Within a partition a consumer keeps commands in order: a channel's commands
keep their order only when every writer derives their partition from the
channel the same way - the channel as a Kafka message key, say.

```ts
const cmd = command.publish({ channel: 'news', data: { text: 'hi' } });
await sql`INSERT INTO centrifugo_outbox (method, payload, partition) VALUES (${cmd.method}, ${cmd.payload}, 0)`;
```

The outbox table's payload column is jsonb, and `cmd.payload` goes into it
as it is: JSON text, which PostgreSQL stores as the object.

- `readonly method: string` - The API method, such as "publish".
- `readonly payload: string` - The request, as JSON text.

#### `toString(): string`

The command as one JSON message: `{"method": ..., "payload": ...}`.

#### `toJSON(): { method: string; payload: RawJSON; }`

The message of toString for JSON.stringify: payload a JSON object.
toString keeps the payload's text exactly - integers past 2^53 included -
where a JSON.stringify of your own parses and writes it again.

### type `Fetch`

```ts
type Fetch = (url: string, init: FetchInit) => Promise<FetchResponse>;
```

The fetch a Client sends with: the runtime's, or one of your own - undici's,
an instrumented one, a fake in tests. Only this much of fetch is used, so
any of them fits without a cast.

### interface `FetchInit`

What a Client passes its fetch: a POST of JSON text.

- `method: 'POST'`
- `headers: Record<string, string>`
- `body: string`
- `redirect: 'manual'`
- `signal: AbortSignal`

### interface `FetchResponse`

What a Client reads of fetch's response: any fetch's Response has it.

- `readonly status: number`
- `readonly type?: string`
- `readonly headers: Headers`
- `readonly body: { getReader(): { read(): Promise<{ done: boolean; value?: Uint8Array; }>; cancel(): Promise<void>; }; } | null`

#### `text(): Promise<string>`

### `USER_AGENT`

```ts
const USER_AGENT = "jscent/1";
```

The User-Agent jscent sends, unless headers give another.

## jscent: errors

Every error is a `CentError`.

- `CentError`
  - `ApiError`
    - `InternalError`
    - `UnknownChannelError`
    - `NotFoundError`
    - `BadRequestError`
    - `NotAvailableError`
    - `TooManyRequestsError`
    - `UnrecoverablePositionError`
    - `ConflictError`
  - `HTTPError`
    - `UnauthorizedError`
  - `DecodeError`
  - `InvalidRequestError`
  - `InvalidConfigError`
  - `ClosedError`
  - `NetworkError`
  - `TimeoutError`
  - `BatchNotSentError`
  - `BatchSentError`
  - `BroadcastFailedChannelsError`
  - `BatchFailedCommandsError`

### `CentError`

```ts
new CentError(message: string, options?: ErrorOptions)
```

The base of every error jscent throws.

- `idempotencyKey: string | undefined` - Set on the error broadcastWithRetry rejects with when no attempt got a reply - a timeout, say - to the key its attempts carried, made for the call when the request had none: Centrifugo may have published, and a retry with this key does not publish twice. Undefined on other errors.

### `ApiError`

```ts
new ApiError(code: number, serverMessage?: string, temporary?: boolean, proMethod?: string)
```

An error of Centrifugo itself: it understood the request and refused it, or
failed to carry it out.

Centrifugo identifies an error by its `code`; `serverMessage` is for people
and may change. Errors with a known code are thrown as the subclass for it -
`instanceof UnknownChannelError` - and any other code as ApiError itself:
Centrifugo adds codes from time to time, so match the ones you handle and
treat the rest by their class.

- `static readonly code: number` - The code subclasses stand for.
- `readonly code: number` - Centrifugo's error code.
- `readonly serverMessage: string` - Centrifugo's message, for people.
- `readonly temporary: boolean` - Set by Centrifugo when the same request may succeed if retried later - a broker being unavailable, a rate limit - not because of the request. It does not mean nothing was done: a publication may have happened, so retry it with the same idempotencyKey. Centrifugo versions before the field existed never set it; `retryable` takes that into account.

#### `static fromCode(code: number, serverMessage?: string, temporary?: boolean, proMethod?: string): ApiError`

The error for code: the subclass of a known code, ApiError otherwise.

### `InternalError`

Code 100: an internal error of Centrifugo, temporary.

- `static readonly code = 100`

### `UnknownChannelError`

Code 102: the channel is not in a namespace Centrifugo is configured with.

- `static readonly code = 102`

### `NotFoundError`

Code 104: what the request refers to was not found.

A method only Centrifugo PRO has, sent in a batch to Centrifugo OSS, fails
with it too, instead of the 404 it gets when sent alone.

- `static readonly code = 104`

### `BadRequestError`

Code 107: Centrifugo refused the request as invalid.

- `static readonly code = 107`

### `NotAvailableError`

Code 108: the feature is not available - history or presence off in the channel's namespace, say.

- `static readonly code = 108`

### `TooManyRequestsError`

Code 111: a rate limit was reached, temporary.

- `static readonly code = 111`

### `UnrecoverablePositionError`

Code 112: the stream position asked for is not in the history any more.

- `static readonly code = 112`

### `ConflictError`

Code 113: the request conflicts with the current state - a map publish whose version check failed, say.

- `static readonly code = 113`

### `HTTPError`

```ts
new HTTPError(status: number, body?: string, headers?: Headers, proMethod?: string)
```

A reply with an HTTP status other than 200: the request did not reach the API
method. A 401 is an UnauthorizedError.

- `readonly status: number` - The reply's HTTP status.
- `readonly body: string` - The start of the reply's body, for diagnostics.
- `readonly headers: Headers` - The reply's headers: a request ID a proxy set, a Retry-After.

### `UnauthorizedError`

A 401: Centrifugo did not accept the credentials - the API key or the bearer token.

### `DecodeError`

The reply is not a Centrifugo API reply. The usual cause is an apiEndpoint
which does not point at Centrifugo's API, so that something else - a proxy,
a web page - answers instead.

### `InvalidRequestError`

A request the client can tell is wrong without sending it: one which cannot
be encoded - a payload which is not JSON, in any request - or a publication
without a channel or data. It is never sent.

Only rules which hold for every Centrifugo are checked; everything else
Centrifugo checks itself, and reports as a BadRequestError.

### `InvalidConfigError`

A configuration with a mistake: the message names the option and the fix.

### `ClosedError`

A call made after the client was closed.

### `NetworkError`

```ts
new NetworkError(message: string, options?: ErrorOptions & { certificate?: boolean; })
```

The request failed on its way: a refused or reset connection, a failed TLS
handshake. The cause is the fetch error.

- `readonly certificate: boolean` - The server's TLS certificate was refused - an unknown CA, an expired certificate, another host's: no retry fixes it, so retryable is false. Told from the fetch error's cause unless given.

### `TimeoutError`

The request timed out: its `timeout`, or `requestTimeout`. A request which
timed out may still have been carried out. A call aborted by its own
`signal` throws the signal's reason instead, as fetch does.

### `BatchNotSentError`

A pending command's result read before its batch was sent.

### `BatchSentError`

A batch sent again: a batch is sent once.

### `BroadcastFailedChannelsError`

```ts
new BroadcastFailedChannelsError(failed: ChannelResult[], total: number, result: BroadcastResult)
```

A broadcast Centrifugo carried out which failed in one or more of its
channels, up to all of them. `result` holds every channel's outcome.

It is not an ApiError of its parts: `instanceof UnknownChannelError` is false
for a broadcast in which one channel of many was unknown, and for one into a
single channel - the broadcast as a whole is not unknown. Look at each
channel's error in `failed`.

- `readonly failed: ChannelResult[]` - The channels which failed, with their errors, in the order of the request.
- `readonly total: number` - How many channels the broadcast had.
- `readonly result: BroadcastResult` - Every channel's outcome.

#### `retryableChannels(): string[]`

The channels whose failure is retryable, in the order of the request: the
channels a retry should go to, with the same idempotencyKey. Channels which
failed for good, such as an unknown channel, are left out.

### `BatchFailedCommandsError`

```ts
new BatchFailedCommandsError(failed: FailedCommand[], total: number, result: BatchResult)
```

A batch in which one or more commands failed, up to all of them. Every
command got its own reply: each Pending holds its outcome. `result` is the
batch's.

It is not an ApiError of its parts: look at each command's error in
`failed`, or at its Pending.

- `readonly failed: FailedCommand[]`
- `readonly total: number`
- `readonly result: BatchResult`

## jscent: HTTP handlers

The framework-free core of every handler, with its Fetch and Node.js adapters.

### interface `HttpRequest`

A request to a handler, as the application's function receives it.

- `readonly method: string` - The HTTP method, upper case.
- `readonly headers: Headers` - The headers: those Centrifugo passes on from the client's connection to a proxy, the client SDK's to an endpoint. `get` is case-insensitive.
- `readonly query: URLSearchParams` - The query parameters.
- `readonly path: string` - The path, as the server saw it.
- `readonly raw: unknown` - The server's own form of the request - the Fetch Request, Node's IncomingMessage, or what was given to handle - for what the core does not carry, such as the client's address or a user your framework authenticated.

### interface `HttpResponse`

A handler's answer.

- `readonly status: number`
- `readonly headers: Record<string, string>`
- `readonly body: string`

### interface `HandleInput`

What handle takes: a request in plain terms.

- `method: string`
- `headers?: HeadersInit | Record<string, string | string[] | undefined>` - Headers as a Headers, an object - Express's req.headers - or pairs.
- `body?: string | Uint8Array`
- `url?: string` - The URL or path with its query: "/centrifugo/connect?x=1".
- `raw?: unknown`

### type `OnError`

```ts
type OnError = (request: HttpRequest, error: unknown) => void;
```

Called with every request answered 400 or 500, and the error. It must not throw.

### interface `NodeRequest`

The parts of Node's IncomingMessage the Node adapter reads. Express's req is one.

- `method?: string`
- `url?: string`
- `headers: Record<string, string | string[] | undefined>`
- `body?: unknown` - Set by a body parser which ran before: express.raw(), express.text() or express.json().

### interface `NodeResponse`

The parts of Node's ServerResponse the Node adapter writes. Express's res is one.

#### `writeHead(status: number, headers: Record<string, string>): unknown`

#### `end(body: string): unknown`

### `Handler`

```ts
new Handler(onError: OnError | undefined, maxBody: number)
```

The base of every handler - a token or signature endpoint, the JWKS
endpoint, a proxy handler. Its framework-free core, `handle`, turns a
request into a response; `fetch` serves it wherever requests are Fetch API
Requests - Cloudflare Workers, Deno, Bun, Hono, Next.js route handlers - and
`node` in node:http and Express.

- `readonly maxBody: number` - The largest request body read, in bytes.
- `readonly fetch: (request: Request) => Promise<Response>` - The handler as a Fetch API function, bound to it: ```ts export default { fetch: handler.fetch }; // Cloudflare Workers, Bun.serve, Deno.serve export const POST = handler.fetch; // a Next.js route handler app.post('/centrifugo/connect', (c) => handler.fetch(c.req.raw)); // Hono ```
- `readonly node: (req: NodeRequest, res: NodeResponse) => Promise<void>` - The handler for node:http and Express, bound to it: ```ts http.createServer(handler.node); app.post('/centrifugo/connect', handler.node); // Express ``` It reads the body itself. Behind a body parser - express.json() - it takes what the parser read: register express.raw() or express.text() on the route to keep the body exactly as Centrifugo sent it.

#### `handle(input: HandleInput): Promise<HttpResponse>`

Answers a request: the core every adapter calls. `raw` is passed on to the
function as HttpRequest.raw: the server's own request object, or what your
framework knows of the request, such as its authenticated user.

## jscent/token

### `NEVER`

```ts
const NEVER: unique symbol;
```

An expiry chosen to be never - always explicitly: for expiresAt, a token
accepted forever, and forever once leaked; for connectionExpiresAt and
subscriptionExpiresAt, a connection or subscription which never expires.

### type `Expiry`

```ts
type Expiry = Date | typeof NEVER;
```

An expiry: a time, or NEVER.

### `Key`

A key signing tokens, matching the one Centrifugo verifies with. Make one
with Key.hmac, Key.fromPem, Key.fromJwk or Key.ed25519.

- `readonly alg: string` - The JWS algorithm: HS256, RS256, ES256, ES384, ES512 or EdDSA.
- `readonly kid: string` - The key ID written as the tokens' "kid", if set.

#### `withKeyId(kid: string): Key`

The key, with `kid` as the "kid" of the tokens it signs: the ID of its
public key in the JWKS Centrifugo verifies with. Never give the ID of a key
to another: Centrifugo caches keys by ID, and would refuse the other key's
tokens until its cache expires.

#### `static hmac(secret: string | Uint8Array): Key`

A key signing with HS256 and secret: Centrifugo's client.token.hmac_secret_key.

#### `static fromPem(pem: string): Promise<Key>`

The key of a PEM-encoded PKCS #8 private key ("BEGIN PRIVATE KEY") - RSA
(RS256), ECDSA on P-256, P-384 or P-521 (ES256, ES384, ES512), or Ed25519
(EdDSA). Convert an older "BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY" or "BEGIN EC PRIVATE
KEY" with `openssl pkcs8 -topk8 -nocrypt`.

#### `static fromJwk(jwk: JsonWebKey): Promise<Key>`

The key of a private JSON Web Key - RSA, EC on P-256, P-384 or P-521, or
OKP Ed25519 - as Key.fromPem makes it.

#### `static ed25519(seed: Uint8Array): Promise<Key>`

A key signing with EdDSA from a 32-byte Ed25519 seed, whose public key is
Centrifugo's client.token.ed25519_public_key (Centrifugo v6.10.2+), or is
published in its JWKS.

### interface `ChannelsCapability`

Operations granted in channels: a connection may do an operation in a channel
when any of its capabilities allows the operation and matches the channel.
Centrifugo PRO only.

- `channels?: readonly string[]` - The channels, or channel patterns, it applies to.
- `allow?: readonly string[]` - The operations: "sub" (subscribe), "pub" (publish), "hst" (history), "prs" (presence).
- `match?: string` - How channels are matched: empty for exact names, "wildcard" or "regex".

### interface `SubscribeOptions`

The options of a server-side subscription in ConnectionClaims.subs.

- `info?: unknown` - Channel-specific information about the connection.
- `b64info?: string` - Binary info in base64, instead of info.
- `data?: unknown` - Sent to the client with the subscription.
- `b64data?: string` - Binary data in base64, instead of data.
- `override?: SubscribeOptionOverride` - Channel options of the namespace overridden for this subscription.
- `serverTagsFilter?: FilterNode` - Only publications whose tags match it are delivered. Centrifugo PRO only, which refuses a malformed filter: the subscription fails.

### interface `ConnectionClaims`

The claims of a connection token. See https://centrifugal.dev/docs/server/authentication.

- `user?: string` - The ID of the connection's user: the "sub" claim. Empty for an anonymous connection.
- `expiresAt: Expiry` - Until when the token is accepted: the "exp" claim, or NEVER for a token accepted forever - and forever once leaked, for a trusted service's own connection, say. Required. The connection expires then too, unless connectionExpiresAt says otherwise: Centrifugo asks the client for a new token, and closes the connection without one.
- `connectionExpiresAt?: Expiry` - When set, when the connection expires instead of at expiresAt: the "expire_at" claim. NEVER makes the connection never expire - Centrifugo never asks for a new token - while expiresAt still bounds when the token is accepted, on reconnects too. Most applications leave it unset.
- `issuedAt?: Date` - The "iat" claim; now when unset.
- `id?: string` - The "jti" claim, for Centrifugo PRO's token revocation.
- `audience?: string` - The "aud" claim: client.token.audience.
- `issuer?: string` - The "iss" claim: client.token.issuer.
- `info?: unknown` - Information about the connection: in presence, join and leave events, and the client's publications.
- `b64info?: string` - Binary info in base64, instead of info.
- `channels?: readonly string[]` - Server-side channels to subscribe the connection to.
- `subs?: Record<string, SubscribeOptions>` - Server-side channels to subscribe the connection to, each with its options. Set channels or subs, not both: Centrifugo ignores channels when subs is set.
- `meta?: unknown` - Custom data attached to the connection. Not visible to other clients - Centrifugo never sends it - but the token carries it, visible to the user owning the token: put nothing in it that user must not see.
- `caps?: readonly ChannelsCapability[]` - Capabilities granting the connection operations in channels. Centrifugo PRO only.
- `labels?: Record<string, string>` - The connection's client labels: for metrics, targeted server API calls and CEL expressions. Centrifugo PRO only.

### interface `SubscriptionClaims`

The claims of a subscription token. See https://centrifugal.dev/docs/server/channel_token_auth.

- `user?: string` - The ID of the connection's user: the "sub" claim.
- `channel: string` - The channel the token allows to subscribe to. Required.
- `expiresAt: Expiry` - Until when the token is accepted: the "exp" claim, or NEVER. Required. The subscription expires then too, unless subscriptionExpiresAt says otherwise.
- `subscriptionExpiresAt?: Expiry` - When set, when the subscription expires instead of at expiresAt: the "expire_at" claim. NEVER makes it never expire, while expiresAt still bounds when the token is accepted: with a short expiresAt, a token which subscribes once.
- `issuedAt?: Date` - The "iat" claim; now when unset.
- `id?: string` - The "jti" claim, for Centrifugo PRO's token revocation.
- `audience?: string` - The "aud" claim.
- `issuer?: string` - The "iss" claim.
- `info?: unknown` - Channel-specific information about the connection.
- `b64info?: string` - Binary info in base64, instead of info.
- `data?: unknown` - Sent to the client in the subscribe reply.
- `b64data?: string` - Binary data in base64, instead of data.
- `override?: SubscribeOptionOverride` - Channel options of the namespace overridden for this subscription.
- `allow?: readonly string[]` - Capabilities in the channel besides subscribing: "pub", "hst", "prs". Centrifugo PRO only.
- `serverTagsFilter?: FilterNode` - Only publications whose tags match it are delivered. Centrifugo PRO only.

### interface `ApiClaims`

The claims of a token authenticating calls to Centrifugo PRO's server API,
verified with the keys of http_api.jwks.endpoint. See
https://centrifugal.dev/docs/pro/server_api_enhancements.

A token passing Centrifugo PRO's checks can call every API method, and it
checks only what it is configured to: the signature by any key of the JWKS
endpoint, and audience, issuer and scope only when http_api.jwks sets them.
So the token must carry a claim no other token carries - above all the
connection and subscription tokens users hold:

- sign API tokens with keys of their own, published at their own JWKS
  endpoint - never the one of client.token.jwks_public_endpoint;
- set audience, scope or both, to values only API tokens carry, and
  configure http_api.jwks.audience and scope to require them. api refuses
  claims with neither.

- `audience?: string` - The "aud" claim: http_api.jwks.audience.
- `scope?: readonly string[]` - The "scope" claim, its scopes joined by spaces: http_api.jwks.scope is one of them.
- `issuer?: string` - The "iss" claim: http_api.jwks.issuer.
- `subject?: string` - The "sub" claim: who calls the API, for the application's own logs.
- `expiresAt?: Date` - When the token expires: required, best minutes ahead. Centrifugo PRO would accept a token without "exp" for as long as its key is published, so api never signs one. ApiTokens sets it itself.
- `issuedAt?: Date` - The "iat" claim; now when unset.
- `id?: string` - The "jti" claim.

### `connection`

```ts
function connection(key: Key, claims: ConnectionClaims): Promise<string>;
```

A connection token with claims, signed with key.

### `subscription`

```ts
function subscription(key: Key, claims: SubscriptionClaims): Promise<string>;
```

A subscription token with claims, signed with key.

### `api`

```ts
function api(key: Key, claims: ApiClaims): Promise<string>;
```

A token for Centrifugo PRO's server API with claims, signed with key - an
asymmetric key with an ID, published by jwks: Centrifugo PRO finds it by the
"kid". See ApiClaims for keeping it apart from client tokens, and ApiTokens
for one to send with every call.

### `jwks`

```ts
function jwks(...keys: Key[]): string;
```

The public keys of keys as a JSON Web Key Set, for Centrifugo's
client.token.jwks_public_endpoint, which verifies tokens by their "kid".
Each key needs an ID - see Key.withKeyId - unique in the set. HMAC keys have
no public key to publish, and are refused, as is a set without keys.

A set is how keys rotate without restarting Centrifugo: publish the new key
next to the old one; once every instance of the application publishes it,
sign with it; drop the old key once the tokens it signed have expired. Never
give a key ID to another key: Centrifugo caches keys by ID.

Publish the keys of client tokens and of Centrifugo PRO's server API tokens
at separate endpoints: a token signed with any key of a set passes
Centrifugo's signature check.

### `ApiTokens`

```ts
new ApiTokens(options: { claims: ApiClaims; key?: Key; currentKey?: () => Key | Promise<Key>; /** Milliseconds a token is valid: 5 minutes by default. */ ttl?: number; })
```

Issues the tokens a Client sends to Centrifugo PRO: its token method is the
client's getBearerToken. It signs a token with api and reuses it for half
its lifetime, so a token sent has at least half of it left.

```ts
const tokens = new ApiTokens({
  key: apiKey,   // its own key, not the client tokens'
  claims: { audience: 'centrifugo-api', scope: ['centrifugo:api'] },
});
const client = new Client({ apiEndpoint, getBearerToken: tokens.token });
```

currentKey, when set, returns the key to sign each new token with instead of
key - the key active now, when keys rotate. A key must be published in the
JWKS before it signs: Centrifugo PRO refuses a token whose key it can't
find. claims must leave expiresAt and issuedAt unset: the tokens are issued
when needed and expire ttl milliseconds later (5 minutes by default).

- `readonly token: () => Promise<string>` - A token valid for at least half of ttl, signing a new one when the previous one has less left. Bound to its ApiTokens: pass it on as it is. Concurrent calls share one signing.

## jscent/endpoints

### `Unauthorized`

```ts
new Unauthorized(message?: string, options?: ErrorOptions)
```

Thrown by the function of an endpoint when the user may not have a token or
signature: answered with 403, on which client SDKs stop asking. It is the
endpoints' own, named after client SDKs' UnauthorizedError - not the API
client's UnauthorizedError, which means Centrifugo refused the SDK's
credentials.

### `ConnectionToken`

```ts
new ConnectionToken(issue: (http: HttpRequest) => string | Promise<string>, options?: { onError?: OnError; })
```

The endpoint a client's getToken callback calls: issue returns the connection
token of the request's user - from connection(), say - or throws
Unauthorized. It takes GET and POST, the body ignored.

```ts
const endpoint = new ConnectionToken(async (http) => {
  const user = await sessionUser(http.headers.get('cookie'));
  if (!user) throw new Unauthorized();
  return token.connection(key, { user, expiresAt: new Date(Date.now() + 15 * 60_000) });
});
```

### `SubscriptionToken`

```ts
new SubscriptionToken(issue: (http: HttpRequest, channel: string) => string | Promise<string>, options?: { onError?: OnError; })
```

The endpoint a subscription's getToken callback calls: issue returns the
token of the request's user for the channel - from subscription(), say - or
throws Unauthorized when the user may not subscribe. The channel comes from
a POST's JSON body, {"channel": ...}, or from a GET's channel query
parameter; it is required.

### interface `SignedKeys`

What a SharedPollSignature function returns: the keys signed, in order, and the signature.

- `keys: readonly string[]`
- `signature: string`

### `SharedPollSignature`

```ts
new SharedPollSignature(sign: (http: HttpRequest, channel: string, keys: string[]) => SignedKeys | Promise<SignedKeys>, options?: { onError?: OnError; })
```

The endpoint a shared poll subscription's getSignature callback calls: a POST
of {"channel": ..., "keys": [...]}, answered {"signature": ..., "keys":
[...]}.

sign decides which of the keys the user may track in the channel, signs them
- with sharedpoll's sign, say - and returns them, in the order signed, with
the signature. The keys it leaves out are revoked: the client stops tracking
them. To end the subscription instead, it throws Unauthorized. It may return
only keys it was asked for: a signature covering another would be refused,
and such a key fails the request with 500.

### `JWKS`

```ts
new JWKS(...keys: Key[])
```

Serves the JSON Web Key Set of keys - see jwks - at the URL configured as
Centrifugo's client.token.jwks_public_endpoint, or Centrifugo PRO's
http_api.jwks.endpoint for API keys. It answers GET and HEAD, cacheable for
five minutes. A set jwks refuses fails here, when the endpoint is built.

## jscent/sharedpoll

### interface `SignOptions`

What sign takes.

- `user: string` - The ID of the connection's user; empty for an anonymous one.
- `channel: string` - The shared poll channel.
- `keys: readonly string[]` - The keys the signature covers, exactly and in their order.
- `expiresAt: Expiry` - When the signature expires: required, as a token's expiry is - a Date, or token.NEVER for a signature which never expires.

### `sign`

```ts
function sign(secret: string | Uint8Array, options: SignOptions): Promise<string>;
```

The signature authorizing a user to track keys in a channel until
expiresAt, as Centrifugo verifies it: "iat:exp:hmac", iat now and exp
expiresAt in Unix seconds - 0 for NEVER, a signature which does not expire.
secret is Centrifugo's shared_poll.hmac_secret_key.

The signature covers exactly keys, in their order: a client tracking other
keys, or the same in another order, is refused.

```ts
await sign(secret, { user: '42', channel: 'poll:prices', keys: ['AAPL'], expiresAt });
```

## jscent/proxy

### `DEFAULT_MAX_BODY`

```ts
const DEFAULT_MAX_BODY: number;
```

The default bound of a request's body, 16 MiB: far above what Centrifugo's
own limits on client messages let through, it only stops a request which is
not Centrifugo's from taking the memory it likes.

### `ProxyError`

```ts
new ProxyError(code: number, message?: string, temporary?: boolean, options?: ErrorOptions)
```

Thrown by a proxy function to reject the client's request with this error: a
code in [400, 1999], which Centrifugo leaves to applications. temporary tells
the client that retrying may succeed.

- `readonly code: number` - The error code: in [400, 1999].
- `readonly temporary: boolean` - Tells the client that retrying may succeed.

### `Disconnect`

```ts
new Disconnect(code: number, reason?: string, options?: ErrorOptions)
```

Thrown by a proxy function to close the client's connection: a code in
[4000, 4999] - [4000, 4499] tells the client to reconnect, [4500, 4999] not
to. reason is a short description, at most 32 bytes.

- `readonly code: number` - The disconnect code: in [4000, 4999].
- `readonly reason: string` - A short description, at most 32 bytes.

### interface `ProxyHandlerOptions`

The options of a proxy handler.

- `onError?: OnError` - Told of every 500 and 400, with the error.
- `maxBody?: number` - The largest request body read: 16 MiB by default.

### `ProxyHandler`

```ts
new ProxyHandler(func: (request: Req, http: HttpRequest) => Res | Promise<Res>, options?: ProxyHandlerOptions)
```

A proxy handler: it decodes the request Centrifugo sends, calls the function
and encodes its answer.

The function returns a result to accept the request, or throws:

- ProxyError rejects the request with that error, which the client
  receives: use codes in [400, 1999]. The connect, subscribe, publish, RPC,
  map publish and map remove proxies pass it to the client; the shared poll
  refresh and channel state proxies take it as a failure.
- Disconnect closes the client's connection with that code: use codes in
  [4000, 4999] - [4500, 4999] to tell the client not to reconnect. Only the
  proxies which pass a ProxyError to the client honour it.
- Any other error, or one a proxy cannot carry, fails the request with HTTP
  status 500, and is passed to onError for logging. Centrifugo then answers
  the client with its temporary internal error; for refresh and sub refresh
  it keeps the connection or subscription for another minute and asks
  again.

A ProxyError or Disconnect as the cause of another error counts too. The
refresh and sub refresh proxies end a connection or subscription through
their result's expired, not an error.

Payloads - data, info, meta - arrive as JSON.parse gives them, and a result
takes them back as they are, or as rawJSON. A proxy with binary_encoding
enabled sends them base64-encoded in the b64 fields, with encoding
"binary"; a result may answer with either field.

Security: Centrifugo trusts what a proxy endpoint answers, and the endpoint
trusts what Centrifugo sends - a SubscribeRequest's user is the user
Centrifugo authenticated. Anyone else able to reach the endpoint could claim
any user. Keep proxy endpoints reachable by Centrifugo only: on an internal
network, or behind a check of a secret Centrifugo sends as a static header.

### `ConnectHandler`

The connect proxy: the function authenticates a connecting client and returns
its user and initial state. ProxyError rejects the connection; Disconnect
closes it with that code.

```ts
const connect = new ConnectHandler(async (req, http) => {
  const user = await sessionUser(http.headers.get('cookie'));   // passed on with http_headers
  if (!user) throw new Disconnect(4501, 'unauthorized');
  return { user };
});
```

### `RefreshHandler`

The refresh proxy: the function decides whether a connection about to expire
lives on, and until when. To end it, return a result with expired set. Any
error fails the request, and Centrifugo keeps the connection for another
minute before asking again.

### `SubscribeHandler`

The subscribe proxy: the function decides whether a client may subscribe to a
channel. ProxyError rejects the subscription; Disconnect closes the
connection.

### `PublishHandler`

The publish proxy: the function decides whether a client may publish into a
channel, and may change the publication. ProxyError rejects it; Disconnect
closes the connection.

### `RPCHandler`

The RPC proxy: the function answers a client's RPC call. ProxyError fails the
call; Disconnect closes the connection.

### `SubRefreshHandler`

The sub refresh proxy: the function decides whether a subscription about to
expire lives on, and until when. To end it, return a result with expired
set. Any error fails the request, and Centrifugo keeps the subscription for
another minute before asking again.

### `MapPublishHandler`

The map publish proxy: the function decides whether a client may publish a
key into a map channel, and may change the publication.

### `MapRemoveHandler`

The map remove proxy: the function decides whether a client may remove a key
from a map channel.

### `SharedPollRefreshHandler`

The shared poll refresh proxy: the function returns the current data of the
items tracked in a shared poll channel. ProxyError, or any other error,
fails the refresh: Centrifugo tries again at the next interval.

### `NotifyCacheEmptyHandler`

The cache empty proxy of Centrifugo PRO: the function learns that a client
subscribed to a channel in cache recovery mode with nothing to recover, and
may publish the current state - then it returns a result with populated set,
for Centrifugo to recover once more. Any error fails the request, and the
client which subscribed is disconnected to reconnect.

### `NotifyChannelStateHandler`

The channel state proxy of Centrifugo PRO, in preview: the function receives
channels becoming occupied or vacated. ProxyError, or any other error, fails
the request.

#### interface `ApnsPushNotification`

ApnsPushNotification is a notification for APNs. Centrifugo PRO only.

- `headers?: Record<string, string>` - The APNs request headers.

#### interface `BlockUserRequest`

BlockUserRequest blocks a user: the user is disconnected and can not
connect again until unblocked or the block expires. Centrifugo PRO only.

- `expireAt?: number` - The Unix time in seconds when the block expires. Optional, but a reasonably small value is recommended to keep the set of blocked users small.
- `user: string` - The ID of the user to block. Required.

#### type `BlockUserResult`

```ts
type BlockUserResult = Record<string, never>;
```

BlockUserResult is the result of a block user call. Empty at the moment.
Centrifugo PRO only.

#### interface `BroadcastRequest`

BroadcastRequest publishes the same data into many channels.

- `channels: readonly string[]` - The list of channels to publish into. Required.
- `data?: unknown` - The payload to publish into each channel. Required unless `b64data` is set. In the HTTP API it is any JSON value; over GRPC it may be binary.
- `b64data?: string` - A base64-encoded binary payload, an alternative to `data` to send binary over the HTTP API. Centrifugo decodes it before publishing.
- `skipHistory?: boolean` - Skips adding the publications to the channels' history.
- `tags?: Record<string, string>` - A map of arbitrary string keys and values attached to each publication and delivered to clients.
- `idempotencyKey?: string` - Drops duplicate publications upon retries. It acts per channel: a broadcast retried with the same key is not published again into the channels which already have it. Results are kept for 5 minutes by default. The memory, Redis and PostgreSQL brokers keep keys; the NATS broker ignores them.
- `delta?: boolean` - Tells Centrifugo to construct a delta update, if possible, when broadcasting the publications to subscribers.
- `version?: number` - When > 0, the version of the document being sent: publications with a version less than or equal to one already seen are ignored. Only works in channels with history enabled.
- `versionEpoch?: string` - The epoch of version. When it changes, Centrifugo accepts the publication even if its version is lower than before.

#### interface `CancelPushRequest`

CancelPushRequest cancels a delayed push notification (sent with
`sendAt`). Centrifugo PRO only.

moment. Centrifugo PRO only.

DisconnectRequest disconnects a user's connections.

- `disconnect?: Disconnect` - A custom disconnect code and reason. If not set, clients are disconnected with a force no-reconnect disconnect.
- `client?: string` - Limits the call to the connection with this client ID. user is still required.
- `whitelist?: readonly string[]` - A list of client IDs to keep connected.
- `session?: string` - Limits the call to the connection with this session ID. user is still required.
- `labelFilter?: FilterNode` - Restricts the call to clients whose labels match this filter. Centrifugo PRO only.
- `allUsers?: boolean` - Works as SubscribeRequest.allUsers. Centrifugo PRO only.

#### interface `FcmPushNotification`

FcmPushNotification is a notification for FCM. Centrifugo PRO only.

#### interface `FilterNode`

FilterNode is a tree describing a predicate over client labels. Used as
`labelFilter` on Subscribe, Unsubscribe, Disconnect, Refresh and
Connections requests. A node is either a leaf comparison (key, cmp, val or
vals) or a logical operation (op) over child nodes.
Centrifugo PRO only: defined here for protocol-surface consistency,
Centrifugo OSS parses it but ignores it.

- `op?: string` - The logical operation of a non-leaf node: "and", "or" or "not". Empty for a leaf node.
- `key?: string` - The label key a leaf node compares.
- `cmp?: string` - The comparison of a leaf node: "eq", "neq", "in", "nin", "ex", "nex", "sw", "ew", "ct", "gt", "gte", "lt" or "lte".
- `val?: string` - The value to compare with, for single-value comparisons.
- `vals?: readonly string[]` - The values to compare with, for "in" and "nin".
- `nodes?: readonly FilterNode[]` - The child nodes of a logical operation.

- `since?: StreamPosition` - Returns publications after this stream position.
- `reverse?: boolean` - Iterates in reverse order, from latest to earliest.
